newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Experts say Metway merger fair-Metway.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Experts say Metway merger fair-Metway.

text.p: Metway Bank Ltd said on Wednesday independent experts agreed that the merger proposal between the bank and the Queensland government owned Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) and Suncorp Finance was fair and reasonable.

Metway said it would acquire Suncorp and QIDC for a combination of cash raised from the issue of Metway securities and to the Queensland government and shares issued to the government equivalent to 297.8 million Metway ordinary shares.

Metway said under the merger 42.8 million ordinary shares are to be issued, plus 100.0 million fully paid subordinated ordinary shares. These shares would rank behind ordinary share for dividend purposes for three years ending June 30, 1999.
It said any dividends declared during this period will first be applied to pay dividends on ordinary shares up to 44 cents per share.

Metway said any dividends declared beyond that level would then be applied to pay dividends on subordinated ordinary shares up to 44 cents a share. It said 155.0 million capital notes would be issued at A$4.50 per note with an interest rate of 8.7 percent per annum. These notes would be convertible into fully paid ordinary shares on a one for one basis at specified dates.

The government has agreed to convert 20 percent of the notes on the third anniversary of the date of issue, 40 percent on the fourth anniversary and all remaining notes within 10 years of issue or when the government has less than 15 percent of Metway voting shares.
Metway said its ordinary shareholders would be offered the choice of retaining their interest in the merged Metway-Suncorp or receiving a cash payment of A$4.80 per share.
The cash payment would be made by the Queensland government through a newly created publicly listed trust, Metway said.
A special dividend of four cents per share would also be paid to all Metway shareholders. This dividend would not be paid if the proposed merger did not proceed, it said.
The Queensland government planned to offer Metway shareholders in December 1998 one ordinary share for every two ordinary shares held at a price of A$5.00 per share, it said.
Metway said shareholders would have a choice of retaining their shareholding in Suncorp-Metway or receiving cash payment of A$4.80 from the Queensland government.
Following the propsed acquisition of Suncorp and QIDC by Metway, the bank would have 284.58 million shares on issue and 155.0 million capital notes, Metway said.
Metway currently has 139.76 million shares on issue.
Metway shares last traded on Tuesday at A$4.79.
